best.hypothesis: Compile the distinct monomial dictionary once, then apply an exact sparse congruence transformation to its Gram map. Reusing coordinate transformations across canonical rows may reduce repeated algebra and coefficient multiplication; no measured improvement is claimed.
best.mechanism: Write O_i = sum_a A_ia W_a. A monomial diagonal contributes A_ia^2 to coordinate (i,i) and 2*A_ia*A_ja to (i,j). A symmetrized monomial pair a<b contributes A_ia*A_ib to (i,i) and A_ia*A_jb+A_ib*A_ja to (i,j). Compile these sparse integer transformations lazily, reuse them for every canonical row, and remove exact cancellations.
best.assumptions: Input coefficients are Python integers; nonzero words satisfy the stated homogeneous-charge and degree constraints. monomial_map supplies the exact canonical map with the specified symmetric convention and stores its backend cache in payload['cache'].
